newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end firmer ahead of key events next week.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end firmer ahead of key events next week.

text.p: Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed firmer on Friday, near a halfway point between Thursday's Tokyo low and the LIFFE high.

Trade was subdued, mainly led by position adjustments before key economic events next week, including fiscal book closings on Monday and the Bank of Japan's quarterly "tankan" corporate survey on Wednesday, traders said.

"The contract's level of around 125.60 is where we feel most confortable now," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit. The June was up 0.40 at 125.65 with a total of 32,383 contracts changing hands.
"The market has calmed down since the June fluctuated wildly on both sides in past sessions," the dealer said.
After a morning rally triggered by dealers' short-covering following an overnight rebound on LIFFE, the contract mostly stayed at around 125.50-125.60 for the rest of the day, dealers said.
Japan's industrial production data released at 0430 GMT had a neutral impact on the market, they said.
The June rose as high as 125.73 by midday. The LIFFE's high was at 125.85 on Thursday after the key contract ended at the day's low of 125.25 in Tokyo.
JGBs fell sharply in Tokyo on Thursday on a media report that Nippon Credit Bank (NCB) may withdraw from overseas operations under a two-stage restructuring plan.

NCB's restructuring, if it is implemented, is seen as a negative factor for JGBs as it would ease worries about Japan's financial system. But in a news conference held later on Thursday, Tadao Iwaki, the bank's senior managing director, denied reports that a restructuring plan had been finalised.
A dealer at a long-term credit bank's securities unit said: "The June was oversold yesterday. But its rebound was weak today as it failed to reach the LIFFE high of 125.85."
But the downside room was also limited as scattered buying was detected on dips from life insurers and banks, he said.

Traders said newly launched Shikoku Electric Power Co Inc's 20-year bond was sold well, another factor providing a firm tone to the JGB market. The bond was launched this afternoon. The coupon rate was at 3.25 percent, instead of the 3.20 percent many had expected.

February's fall of 3.4 percent in Japan's industrial output was within expectations. But a forecast of a decline of 0.2 percent in March and a rise of 1.0 percent in April triggered an initial reaction of selling, which was followed by buying.
"Although April is a positive figure, the production level is forecast to be lower than it was in January," said Yasunari Ueno, chief market economist at Fuji Securities.
The yield of the key 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.295 percent, down 0.005 from Thursday's finish.
Traders said they will be focusing on whether other Japanese banks may have to share the burden of ailing NCB.

NCB said on Thursday it could not give a specific date to unveil the restructuring plan. But the plan might be announced before NCB sets terms of April debenture on April 9, traders said. -- R.Maeda Tokyo Treasury +81-3-3432-8570
